transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Yeah, nice to meet you too. I guess I'm here because... well, the main thing is I just get pulled off track by every little sound or thought. Like, I’ll be trying to work on a job application, right? And then I'll hear a car outside. Which has been super annoying lately because my neighbor just bought this ridiculously loud Mustang. It's like bright yellow, and he revs it at all hours of the day. I don't even know how he affords it, honestly, because I'm pretty sure he just works at the grocery store down the street. The one that used to be a Blockbuster? Man, I miss Blockbuster. Just walking around the aisles and getting the candy in those little boxes... 

Wait, what was I saying? Oh, right, the application. Yeah, so I'll be trying
Have there been times when you felt unusually high, energized, or on top of the world?

High or on top of the world? Uh, no, I don't think so. I mean, unless you count when I drink way too much caffeine. Like the other day I got a couple of those new energy drinks, the ones that taste like Sour Patch Kids? Man, those things are dangerous. They taste exactly like the blue candy. I used to eat so much of that candy when I worked at the warehouse a couple years ago. That job was awful, by the way. Just standing on concrete for ten hours scanning boxes. My manager, Dave, he was this super intense guy who always wore sunglasses indoors. Who does that, right? He said it was because the fluorescent lights gave him a headache, but I'm pretty sure he just thought he looked cool, like the Terminator or something. He actually drove a motorcycle to work every day, even when it was raining. 

Anyway, I don't even know why I brought up Dave... what did you ask me? Something about feeling energized? But yeah, no, I
Do you ever hear voices when no one is there?

Voices? Like, hearing things? No, definitely not. I mean, I hear my own thoughts, obviously. Sometimes they're really loud, especially when I'm trying to sleep. That's the worst, right? You lay down and suddenly your brain is like, "Hey, remember that embarrassing thing you did in fifth grade?" For me, it was the talent show. I tried to do a magic trick with this disappearing coin, but I dropped it and it rolled all the way off the stage and hit the principal's shoe. Mr. Henderson. He had these really shiny loafers. I always wondered how he kept them so clean, because the parking lot was gravel back then. They paved it my senior year, which was a nightmare because the tar smell was everywhere for like a week. I couldn't even eat my lunch outside. 

Wait, what did you ask me? Oh, voices. Yeah, no, I don't hear anything like that. Just my own brain never shutting up.
Did these problems with getting distracted and losing your train of thought start when you were a child?

Yeah, for sure. Even back in elementary school, my teachers were always moving my seat around. It was like a weekly thing because I was always talking out of turn, or I'd forget my homework at home, or I'd just rush through the worksheets and make all these stupid careless mistakes. I remember Mrs. Davis in fourth grade put my desk right next to her giant metal filing cabinet. That thing was so old, the bottom drawer was completely rusted shut. I know because I tried to kick it open once when I dropped my pencil under it. It was one of those cool bendy pencils? Man, those things were the best. You couldn't actually write with them because the graphite would just snap, but they were so fun to twist up into knots. I got
Do you spend a lot of time worrying about things, even when there isn’t an immediate problem?

Worrying? I mean, not really. I don't sit around stressing about things that haven't happened. I actually try not to think too far ahead because then I just get overwhelmed. Like last week, I was trying to figure out if I should finally fix my car—it's this 2008 Honda Civic, and the AC has been busted for like three years. Summer is brutal. You roll the windows down, but then you can't hear the radio. And I need the radio because I listen to this one morning show where they do these prank calls. They had this one guy call a pizza place and try to order a tire. The guy at the pizza place was getting so mad, it was hilarious. I actually used to deliver pizzas for a few months right after high school. Worst job ever. The smell of pepperoni just gets stuck in your car's upholstery, you know? I tried everything to get it out—baking soda, those little pine tree air fresheners. I bought like five of the "Black Ice" ones and hung them all on the rearview mirror. 

Wait, what were we talking about? Oh, worrying. Yeah, no, I don't really worry about stuff unless it's like, right in front of my face.
